missionPremise: Three cards in one session on operator authority: G-89 the lens flash first because it is what a prospect sees, G-88 items 4 and 5 as one coupled lane because the kit's SHIPPED.size===109 pin was passing on a stale vendored stylesheet, and G-88 items 6/7/9/10 the design pass, of which item 7 was the only acceptance item in the eleven-item WDLL with no instrument behind it. The governing habit carried in from the prior session: three premises the work was scoped on had been measured false, each caught by an executor measuring rather than reasoning. When a card tells you WHY, check the why before you build the what.
completionPredicate: G-89 merged, deployed and proven by a probe watched failing on the pre-fix build. G-88 item 4 recounted rather than forecast. Item 5 wrapped and re-synced with sentinel first and _ds_sync.json last and alone. Item 7 merged with a test that fails on a removed id. Items 6, 9 and 10 shipped surface by surface and walked. The last three did not happen and are held, not dropped.
scopeBasis: Items 1, 2, 3, 8 and 11 of the WDLL were already done or standing. Item 6 depends on item 5, so the design pass could not start until the kit wrapped the four families; item 7 depends only on item 3, which was done, so it parallelised. That dependency reading is what made three concurrent executors correct rather than two serial ones.

findingsWorthKeeping.title: WDLL item 10's acceptance walk cannot see what it is written to check
findingsWorthKeeping.detail: The served document is byte-identical across every lens and every pack — six URL forms, one sha256. Item 10 as written is thirteen identical GETs then thirteen more, and would pass identically on a redesigned build and an untouched one. Replaced with three legs: deployed-bytes hash against the merged tree, pack checks moved to /api/*, and a real browser walk, which is the only leg that can grade a design pass.

findingsWorthKeeping.title: A green check-run plus a CLEAN merge state is not a merge gate
findingsWorthKeeping.detail: Demonstrated twice in one hour, once inside a repo and once across two. A check-run conclusion is a statement about the PR's tree; CLEAN is a statement about textual conflict; neither is a statement about the tree that exists after the merge. Merging either PR on its own green would have broken main.

findingsWorthKeeping.title: The kit's injection harness was proving the wrong arm
findingsWorthKeeping.detail: The case labelled `vendor parity arm B` edits vendor/shell.css, which breaks the PIN — arm A — and its needle was arm A's own message. Arm B is the only guardrail that can see the PRODUCT move, it is the one that went red for real this session, and it had no injection at all. Relabelled, and a real arm B case added that edits nothing and builds a divergent upstream checkout instead.

findingsWorthKeeping.title: conventions.md was telling the design agent the four families had no CSS

findingsWorthKeeping.title: A browser probe that reads the DOM before the render-blocking stylesheet applies reports total CSS failure
findingsWorthKeeping.detail: The planner's own edge probe, run with javaScriptEnabled false and waitUntil domcontentloaded, reported all 15 sections visible — indistinguishable from a catastrophic regression. document.styleSheets.length was 1 instead of 3 and body background was transparent. Waiting for load fixed it and the case passes. The product was never wrong. Recorded because this is the second planner instrument this session that measured something other than what it was written to measure.

findingsWorthKeeping.title: A mutation that does not apply is indistinguishable from an instrument that does not fire
findingsWorthKeeping.detail: Three planner mutations this session silently failed to apply: one hit a CSS comment rather than the rule, one hit a generator rather than the served document, and one used an LF regex against a CRLF checkout. Each produced a green result that reads exactly like a working system. The habit that caught all three was echoing the byte count or occurrence count the mutation claimed to change.

rulingsTaken.ruling: The root attribute ships as data-surface, not A-072's data-lens.
rulingsTaken.why: data-lens already exists in the document on the fifteen nav anchors carrying a different value vocabulary — the bare lens id, where the root needs the section id. Two vocabularies under one attribute name is the naming trap, and html[data-lens] would start matching any future querySelectorAll for [data-lens]. A-072's wording was planner scoping language, not an operator ruling on the name.

rulingsTaken.ruling: The G-89 fix extends to the six Development-services tabs and the three Assets tabs.
rulingsTaken.why: Same mechanism one altitude down: #tab-pipeline and #atab-inventory also carry class="on" statically, so ?lens=development-services&tab=review — the dispatch's own acceptance input — would have painted the right lens and then still swapped a populated Pipeline table out for Review.

rulingsTaken.ruling: `rail` keeps its three meanings and is not renamed.
rulingsTaken.why: It now covers the .srcreg severity rail, the .colstack.rail 380px layout modifier, and the new .mxrow > .rail and .finding > .rail. No CSS conflict, every rule scoped. Renaming a shipped class is a product-line change across three byte-locked repos, not a kit PR.
